Fix equality comparisons in boltons.setutils.IndexedSet.

At this snapshot, IndexedSet([1, 2]) compares unequal to another IndexedSet([1, 2]), and comparisons with different contents or ordering can report equality instead.

Two IndexedSet objects should compare their elements in order. Comparisons with a normal set should reflect the same members. Preserve the public ordered-set API and return a Boolean result when an operand contains unhashable nested items, rather than reporting equality for an invalid comparison.
source_basis: Original IndexedSet ordered-set docstring in boltons/setutils.py
Original fixed upstream tests/test_setutils.py equality assertions

TinyDB can return a document from a repeated query even after that document has been deleted.

Reproduce with a table containing one matching document: run a query, remove the document by its ID, then repeat the same query. The stored table is empty and the repeated query should return an empty list. This should work with both MemoryStorage and JSONStorage, while preserving ordinary inserts, updates, and nonempty query behavior.
visible_prompt_profile.source_basis: Actual source-bound run001 MemoryStorage observation, public query/remove API contract and unchanged source test specification; no reference edit or required-ID list supplied in the prompt.

Fix child-process liveness reporting in ptyprocess.PtyProcess.

A newly started child that is still running can be reported as dead. After a child finishes, liveness and termination status can also become inconsistent.

Querying a live child should not wait for it to finish. Report running children as alive and completed or terminated children as dead, while preserving the observed exit or signal status. Preserve the existing process-control API and normal cleanup behavior.
source_basis: Original PtyProcess.isalive docstring and process-control API
Fixed upstream tests/test_wait.py and tests/test_spawn.py behavior
Actual source-bound run001 liveness and reaping observations

Fix transaction-context behavior in dataset.Database.

When an exception leaves a transaction scope, writes made inside that scope can be kept instead of discarded.

Successful transaction scopes should keep their writes. Failed scopes should leave previously committed data unchanged and propagate the original failure. A failed commit should also leave the transaction cleaned up, so later operations and connection cleanup remain usable.
source_basis: Actual run001 source-bound SQLite aborted/committed transaction observations
